title: Canonical ComputerAction proposal IR and model adapters
objective: Define and implement a provider-neutral ComputerActionProposal IR plus separately testable model-specific parsers/adapters, beginning with the pinned UI-TARS action-parser concepts where useful. Adapters normalize untrusted syntax into proposals only; they cannot mint or override Quntal identities, approvals, leases, trust, policy, risk classes, targets, execution outcomes, or remote reach.

include: canonical bounded ComputerActionProposal schema for supported browser, structured desktop, and coordinate proposal kinds
strict source-adapter/version metadata and bounded raw-input provenance without secret retention
UI-TARS adapter using selected action-parser concepts/code only after provenance/license qualification
adapter registry that is explicit, versioned, locally configured, and default-deny for unknown adapters/actions/fields
normalization of model coordinates/boxes into proposal-space values without producing executable target identity or lease authority
schema validation, maximum sizes/counts/text lengths, malformed/ambiguous action rejection, unknown-field widening denial, and deterministic parser errors
differential/fuzz/property tests proving equivalent inputs normalize consistently and adversarial inputs cannot smuggle authority-bearing fields
tests proving every executable action still passes through quntald target revalidation, policy, approval, lease, and postcondition gates
exclude: adapter-issued approvals, trust, target IDs, leases, policy revisions, or execution claims

authority_delta.browser: None beyond converting model syntax into untrusted proposals for already-authorized browser shapes.
authority_delta.ui_input: None beyond proposals; adapters never execute input.
authority_delta.secrets: Raw model payload retention is bounded/minimized and must not add secret-bearing logs.
authority_delta.approval: None; adapters cannot approve or influence approval authority beyond requesting a proposal that the kernel classifies independently.

invariants: all server identities and leases are minted only by Quntal
no adapter directly reaches an execution backend

acceptance.claim: A canonical proposal schema represents every currently supported computer-use action without carrying authority-bearing approval/trust/lease/server-target fields.
The UI-TARS adapter and any additional authorized adapters pass deterministic corpus, boundary, fuzz/property, malformed, unknown-field, and adversarial authority-smuggling tests.
End-to-end tests prove an adapter proposal cannot execute without independent Quntal target resolution/revalidation, policy, approval, lease where applicable, and postcondition handling.
No raw JS/CDP/UIA/input primitive, direct backend call, adapter self-approval, or remote widening is reachable.
Exact-head CI, TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, security review, parser fuzz/property qualification, and zero unresolved blockers pass.

successor_requirements.sg_000084: Remote computer-use mapping may proceed only after provider/model syntax is cleanly separated from local authority.

done_when: Provider/model computer-use syntax is normalized through a canonical untrusted proposal IR with no path for adapters to mint, widen, or execute authority.
